headline: GitHub allows immediate, unreviewed production access for external users with zero mandatory approval.
summary: Developers can instantly register an OAuth App or GitHub App to authenticate external users and interact with the GitHub API. No manual review, security assessment, or test-user whitelisting is required for direct integration. While listing on the GitHub Marketplace is optional and requires a review, applications can be fully deployed and authorized by any user immediately upon creation.

oauth.pkce: Supported for authorization code flows using code_challenge_method=S256.
oauth.refresh_tokens: Standard OAuth App tokens do not expire by default. If expiration is enabled (standard on GitHub Apps), access tokens expire in 8 hours and refresh tokens in 6 months. Refreshing rotates both tokens.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Strict matching of host, port, and path, or a subpath of the registered callback. Loopback IP addresses (127.0.0.1 and ::1) are permitted to vary the port.
oauth.scopes: OAuth Apps use scopes like repo and public_repo. GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions.

steps.title: Create OAuth or GitHub App
steps.detail: Navigate to the Developer settings and register a new application, providing valid redirect URLs, an app name, and a homepage URL.

steps.title: Set App Visibility
steps.detail: If using a GitHub App, navigate to Advanced > Danger zone and set the application's visibility to Public to allow external users to install it.

steps.title: Implement Authorization Flow
steps.detail: Configure the AI agent to redirect users to the authorize endpoint, passing PKCE parameters and requesting required scopes.

steps.title: Handle Callback and Token Exchange
steps.detail: Implement the redirect URI handler to exchange the authorization code and PKCE verifier for access and refresh tokens.

requirements.text: Valid redirect URLs, app name, and homepage URL are required to register an application.
GitHub Apps must be explicitly configured with Public visibility under Advanced settings to be installed by external users.
Organization accounts, enforced 2FA, verified domains, and substantive integration functionality are required only if opting to list on the GitHub Marketplace.

gotchas.text: GitHub does not publish standard OAuth/OIDC discovery metadata documents at its root.
Signing in the same user more than 10 times in one hour triggers a loop protection mechanism, requiring the user to manually re-authorize.
Accessing repositories owned by an organization requires an organization owner's explicit approval if the organization has enabled third-party application restrictions.
OAuth App tokens do not expire by default, but if token expiration is enabled, access tokens expire in 8 hours and refresh tokens in 6 months.

permissions.action: access user repositories and create pull requests
permissions.review_impact: Requesting the repo scope yields broad write access. It triggers organization owner approval during authorization if the target repository belongs to an organization with third-party restrictions enabled. No mandatory GitHub review or paid plan is required.

blockers.issue: Organization owner approval is required to access restricted repositories.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Instruct the user to request approval during the OAuth flow, or contact their organization administrator directly to approve the application in the organization's Third-party access settings.

blockers.issue: Optional GitHub Marketplace listing application is rejected due to insufficient value beyond auth.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Bypass the Marketplace and use a direct OAuth integration, or build additional workflows into your app before resubmitting.

agent_can: Read technical documentation to map endpoint URLs and parameters
Implement the authorization code flow with PKCE and token exchange logic
Draft the required Privacy Policy and Terms of Service if pursuing a Marketplace listing
you_must: Create the application in your GitHub Developer settings
Define the application's redirect URIs and base configuration
Publish the GitHub App via the Danger zone settings for public use

key_claims.text: GitHub does not require any review, verification, or approval before arbitrary external users can authorize an OAuth App or install a public GitHub App.
GitHub's authorization endpoint requires authentication to access developer settings but actively validates OAuth parameters.

open_questions: What is the average review time for an optional GitHub Marketplace listing?
assumptions: Hands-on time estimates assume a standard setup for direct OAuth usage without pursuing an optional Marketplace listing.
Developers will primarily use standard OAuth Apps or public GitHub Apps rather than pursuing publisher verification.
